```text
REVIEW_DECISION: REJECT
RISK_CLASS: high-impact
SUMMARY: The prose contracts are sound: Factory-owned apply/gates/integration, profiles as adapters only, unavailable-not-zero telemetry, 200k/500k as warning not cancellation, non-Sol/Opus refactor review, and proposed-until-reviewed status. The two canonical schemas, however, fail to enforce two of the safety properties they exist to guarantee. The RCA schema lets an author select the model-blaming primary cause without ever setting the flag that triggers the counterfactual-evidence requirement, so blame-by-default validates cleanly. The provenance schema records exactly one reviewer, so the mandatory independent Sol AND Opus approval for acceptance/integration/token-accounting changes is unrepresentable and unverifiable. Both are schema defects present in this package, not unbuilt implementation.
FINDING: high|docs/factory-ng/schemas/factory.root-cause-analysis-v1.schema.json|The counterfactual guard is keyed on the optional boolean `model_profile_causal_claim`, not on `primary_cause`. Setting `primary_cause: "skill_or_model_profile"` while omitting the boolean skips the `allOf/if-then` entirely, so counterfactual_evidence is never required; the enum also fuses Skill defects with profile defects, so a Skill-caused failure is recorded as partial model blame.|Violates required safety property 4: RCA may blame a model without counterfactual evidence, and the prose restriction in change-provenance-and-rca-contract-v1.md has no machine enforcement despite the schema being declared canonical.
REQUIRED_CHANGE: (1) RCA schema: replace the boolean-keyed guard with `{"if": {"properties": {"primary_cause": {"const": "skill_or_model_profile"}}, "required": ["primary_cause"]}, "then": {"required": ["model_profile_causal_claim", "counterfactual_evidence"], "properties": {"model_profile_causal_claim": {"const": true}, "counterfactual_evidence": {"minItems": 1}}}}`, and split the enum into `skill` and `model_profile` so only the latter carries the guard; add a fixture asserting that a record with `primary_cause: "skill_or_model_profile"` and no counterfactual_evidence FAILS validation. (2) Provenance schema: replace the single `review` object with `reviews` (array, minItems 1, each with decision/reviewer_profile/review_sha256), add `contract_change_scope` (`none|amendment|identity_acceptance_integration_or_accounting`), and add a conditional requiring two accepted reviews from distinct reviewer_profiles — one Sol, one Opus — whenever change_class is `factory` or contract_change_scope is the escalated value; add passing/failing fixtures for a token-accounting change with one vs. two approvals. (3) medium|docs/factory-ng/model-profile-contract-v1.md: ship `schemas/factory.model-profile-v1.schema.json` and `factory.execution-receipt/v1` (both referenced but absent), and define `extends` semantics so a child profile may narrow but never override the parent `authority` block (`model_edits_workspace`, `harness_applies_patch`, `harness_owns_tests_and_gates`, `commit_push_deploy`) or `warning_is_hard_stop`; otherwise property 2 rests on prose only.
COUNTEREXAMPLE: Fixture 1, executed against the pinned schemas: a qwen-prepared-local patch passes the visible test and fails the hidden holdout because the gate set omitted the holdout. An author submits `{"schema":"factory.root-cause-analysis/v1","incident_id":"inc-1","provenance_sha256":"sha256:ab…","primary_cause":"skill_or_model_profile","evidence":["holdout failed"],"corrective_ticket_ids":[],"status":"open"}` — no `model_profile_causal_claim`, no `counterfactual_evidence`. The `if` clause requires that property, so it does not match, `then` never applies, and the record validates: Qwen is recorded as primary cause with zero counterfactual evidence, while the correct `harness_or_gate` cause is never forced into consideration. Fixture 5 in the same package: a token-accounting semantics change is committed with a provenance record carrying `review.reviewer_profile: "sol-review@1.0.0"` only; the schema requires exactly one reviewer, so this record is indistinguishable from a dual-approved one and passes every declared check despite the governance text demanding independent Sol and Opus approval.
```
